# Sourdough starter

The starter lives in a glass jar on the kitchen shelf. I feed it every morning with equal weights of flour and water, and it rewards a steady daily rhythm: miss two days and it turns sluggish and sour. At room temperature it doubles in about six hours, and the bubbles tell me when it is ready.

Feeding means discarding most of it first, which feels wasteful until you bake pancakes with the discard. A healthy culture smells of apples and yeast. I keep a small spare jar in the fridge as insurance and refresh it once a week.

Bread made with it needs a long, cool proof overnight. Patience is the main ingredient; a warm shortcut gives a flat loaf with little flavour.
